newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firmer on bourse capital inflow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firmer on bourse capital inflow.

text.p: The Mexican peso reversed earlier softness to close slightly firmer on Wednesday due to foreign traders switching from dollars to invest in the local bourse, traders said.

"The market was very quiet and with dollars in moderate supply from foreign investors stepping into the bourse," a dealer said. The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed one and 0.9 of a centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.8830/7.8880 and 7.8820/7.8850 per dollar.
The IPC index of Mexican stocks was up 1.42 percent at 3,859.26 points when the foreign exchnage market closed.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 1.2 centavos weaker at 7.8870/7.8900 per dollar.
Traders said that although Tuesday night's gains in primary rates were lower than expected, they still helped offset the adverse effects of higher yields on U.S. long bonds.
"I feel the results of last night's Cetes auction were not bad, as you cannot give real interest rates as high as were expected," the trader added.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was off 2/32 in late trade to yield 7.10 percent, compared with being off 14/32 in earlier dealing.
